resources.string: Drawn gap area inside the satellite glial sheath
Radius to the inner edge of the sheath: %1$s u
For soma radius r and gap width w, the inner edge of the sheath sits at radius r + w. Gap area = π × [(r + w)² − r²]. Lengths use arbitrary drawing units (u); areas use square drawing units (u²).

Flattened satellite glial cells form a sheath around a sensory neuron body in a dorsal root ganglion, next to the narrow extracellular space they help regulate. In this schematic cross-section the inner circle is the neuron body and the outer circle is the inner edge of the glial sheath. Only the space between the two lines is counted; it is neither the sheath itself nor axonal myelin. The gap is exaggerated, and no real dimensions are implied.
